福爾摩沙小導遊臺南 Tainan・中西區

延平郡王祠Koxinga Shrine

認識生於日本的國姓爺鄭成功，看這座祠如何從民間小廟、清朝專祠、日本神社，變成今天的北方宮殿式祠堂。

Meet Koxinga, born in Japan, and see how his shrine changed from a folk temple to a palace-style hall.

紅牆綠瓦之後，臺南人在這裡紀念把荷蘭人趕出臺灣的人。鄭成功 1624 年生於日本平戶，父親是華人海商，母親是日本人。明朝皇帝賜他國姓，人稱國姓爺，後來又受封為延平郡王。1661 年船隊渡海來臺，1662 年初荷蘭人投降，但幾個月後鄭成功就病逝了。百姓先蓋小廟紀念他；1875 年清朝建官方專祠，1897 年日本改為開山神社。1963 年改建成北方宮殿式。後殿祭祀他的母親，殿前種著老梅樹。

Behind tall red walls and green glazed tiles, Tainan honors the man who drove the Dutch out of Taiwan. Zheng Chenggong was born in Hirado, Japan, in 1624. His father was a Chinese sea merchant, and his mother was Japanese. The Ming emperor gave him the royal surname, so people called him Koxinga. Later he became the Prince of Yanping. In 1661 his fleet crossed to Taiwan. Early in 1662 the Dutch surrendered, but Koxinga died just a few months later. Local people first honored him in a small temple. In 1875 the Qing built an official shrine, and in 1897 Japan made it a Shinto shrine. In 1963 it was rebuilt as a northern palace. His mother is honored in the rear hall, beside the old plum trees.

為什麼值得來

Why it matters & history
  1. 國姓爺是誰？鄭成功 1624 年生於日本平戶，1662 年在臺灣過世。Zheng Chenggong was born in Japan in 1624 and died in Taiwan in 1662.
  2. 一座祠，四個名字從民間小廟到官方祠堂，政權換了，名字也跟著換。Each new government gave the shrine a new name.
  3. 走進祠堂看一看穿過三川門，前有正殿，後有太妃祠，兩側是長廊。Walk through the gate to the main hall, the rear hall and the long side halls.

認識景點

About the place

國姓爺是誰？Who was Koxinga?

生在日本平戶：父親是海商鄭芝龍，母親是日本人田川氏，小名福松，七歲左右才回到福建。 國姓爺：1645 年南明隆武帝賜他國姓「朱」，並改名「成功」，人稱國姓爺。 延平郡王：南明永曆帝封他為延平郡王，這座祠的名字就是從這裡來的。 1661 年渡海：1661 年率大批戰船從金門出發，進入臺江攻打荷蘭人。

Born in Hirado: His father was a sea merchant and his mother was Japanese. He moved to China at about seven. Lord with the imperial surname: In 1645 the Ming emperor gave him the royal surname, Zhu, and the name Chenggong. Prince of Yanping: The Ming court made him Prince of Yanping, which gave this shrine its name. Crossing in 1661: In 1661 he led a huge fleet from Kinmen to attack the Dutch.

荷蘭人投降：1662 年 2 月 1 日，荷蘭長官揆一交出熱蘭遮城。 英年早逝：同年 6 月，鄭成功病逝，年僅三十多歲。

The Dutch surrender: On February 1, 1662, the Dutch surrendered Fort Zeelandia. An early death: That June, Koxinga died of illness. He was only thirty-seven.

一座祠，四個名字One shrine, four names

開山王廟：相傳鄭成功過世後，臺南百姓蓋了小廟紀念這位「開山王」。 沈葆楨上奏：牡丹社事件後沈葆楨來臺，1875 年朝廷准他為鄭成功建專祠、列入祀典。 福州式祠堂：1875 年從福州請來匠師、運來建材，蓋成「明延平郡王祠」。 開山神社：1897 年日本政府把它改為開山神社，是臺灣第一座神社；原因之一是鄭成功的母親是日本人。

Kaishan Wang Temple: Legend says local people built a small temple for him after he died. Shen Baozhen's petition: In 1875, the Qing court agreed to his petition for an official shrine. A Fuzhou-style shrine: Craftsmen and materials came from Fuzhou to build it. Kaishan Shinto Shrine: In 1897, Japan made it Taiwan's first Shinto shrine, because Koxinga's mother was Japanese.

北方宮殿式：1963 年以鋼筋混凝土改建，1964 年完工，福州式原貌從此消失。

Northern palace style: In 1963 it was rebuilt in concrete, and the Fuzhou look was lost.

走進祠堂看一看Look around the shrine

正殿鄭成功像：正殿中央是雕塑家楊英風在 1961 年創作的鄭成功像，兩旁有沈葆楨題的名聯。他的號是「呦呦」，取自《詩經》「呦呦鹿鳴」，英文名 Yuyu 就是這樣來的。 兩位將軍：大門兩側另有祠，祭祀甘輝與張萬禮兩位將軍。 東西廡牌位：東西兩廡排著上百位明鄭忠臣的牌位，例如陳永華、沈光文。 太妃祠：後殿祭祀母親田川氏；父親鄭芝龍降清，所以不在這裡。

Koxinga's statue: The statue in the main hall was made by the sculptor Yuyu Yang in 1961. His art name Yuyu comes from an old poem about deer calling to friends. Two generals: Small shrines by the gate honor generals Gan Hui and Zhang Wanli. Rows of spirit tablets: The side halls hold spirit tablets for more than a hundred loyal followers. His mother's shrine: The rear hall honors his mother. His father surrendered to the Qing, so he is not here.

再生梅：太妃祠前有梅樹，相傳其中一棵是鄭成功親手種的。 騎馬石像：外庭有 2008 年泉州贈送的巨大花崗石鄭成功騎馬像，旁邊還有形如金門的池子。

The plum trees: Legend says Koxinga planted one of the plum trees himself. The horseback statue: A giant granite Koxinga on horseback stands in the garden near a Kinmen-shaped pond.

實景照片

Photos on site

騎馬石像 Koxinga on horseback

祠旁的庭園裡，有一座很大的石雕：鄭成功穿著盔甲、騎在馬上，手握著劍。

In the garden stands a huge stone statue of Koxinga on horseback. He wears armor and holds a sword.

忠肝義膽石坊 A loyal heart, a brave spirit

往祠堂走，先經過這座花崗石石坊。橫樑上刻著「忠肝義膽」（由右往左讀），意思是「忠心又勇敢」；落款是白崇禧。從石坊望過去，就是下一道大門。

On the way in, you pass under this granite gateway. The words on top read from right to left: a loyal heart and a brave spirit. Look through it to see the next gate.

鳥居的石樑 Stones from a torii

路旁這兩塊又長又彎的石頭，可能是日本時代「開山神社」石鳥居最上面的橫樑（笠木與島木）。這座石鳥居建於 1915 年，後來被拆下，石頭才移到這裡。

These long curved stones were probably the top beams of a torii, a Japanese shrine gate. The stone torii was built in 1915, when this place was a Japanese shrine. Later it was taken down, and the stones were moved here.

鳥居石樑的解說牌 The sign beside the torii stones

石樑旁的解說牌畫出 1915 年開山神社的平面圖。牌上說，這兩塊石頭可能是第一代開山神社石鳥居上方的笠木與島木，神社拆除後才移到這裡。

The sign beside the stones shows a plan of the Shinto shrine in 1915. It says the two stones were probably the top beams of its first stone torii, moved here after the shrine was taken down.

前無古人 No one like him before

大門上的匾寫著「前無古人」（由右往左讀），意思是「在他之前，沒有人像他一樣」。匾上的小字寫著「光緒元年」，也就是 1875 年。右下方的紅字石碑「奉旨祀典」，表示皇帝准許在這裡正式祭祀。

The plaque says: no one before him was like him. Its small words give the year 1875. The red stone marker below says the emperor allowed official worship here.

中庭與正殿 The courtyard and main hall

走進大門，一條石板路直直穿過中庭，通到正殿。1963 年，祠堂改建成中國北方宮殿式的樣子，屋頂鋪著綠色琉璃瓦，兩旁是長長的廊屋。

Inside the gate, a stone path leads across the courtyard to the main hall. In 1963 the shrine was rebuilt in a northern Chinese palace style, with green glazed tiles on the roofs.

中庭兩側的長廊 The long side corridors

穿過三川門，中庭前面是正殿，兩側是長長的迴廊。現在的建築是 1963 年改建的北方宮殿式。

Past the main gate, the courtyard leads to the main hall, with long corridors on both sides. Today's buildings date from the 1963 rebuild in northern palace style.

正殿的鄭成功像 Koxinga in the main hall

正殿中間坐著鄭成功，穿著綠色的袍子，胸前有一條金龍。上方的匾寫著「明延平王」（由右往左讀）。兩旁的燈上寫著「開山王廟」，這是祠堂從前的名字。這尊鄭成功像是雕塑家楊英風在 1961 年創作的。

In the main hall, Koxinga sits in a green robe with a golden dragon. The plaque above says Ming Prince of Yanping. The lanterns show an old name of the shrine, Kaishan Wang Temple. This statue of Koxinga was made by the sculptor Yuyu Yang in 1961.

光緒元年的聖旨 The emperor's order of 1875

正殿裡的金色匾額，刻著光緒元年（1875）正月初十的上諭全文：沈葆楨等人奏請為鄭成功建祠，皇帝准許在臺灣府城（今臺南）建立專祠，並追贈謚號。

This golden board in the main hall shows the emperor's order from 1875. Shen Baozhen had asked for a shrine for Koxinga, and the emperor agreed to build one in Tainan.

誥命箱 The golden edict box

正殿上方掛著金色的「誥命箱」，雕著九條金龍。當年皇帝准許建祠的聖旨就裝在這個箱子裡，聖旨真跡現在收藏在國立臺灣歷史博物館。抬頭看，天花板每一格都有一個藍色圓圈，裡面畫著一條金龍！

A golden box carved with nine dragons hangs in the main hall. It once held the emperor's order to build the shrine. The real order is now kept at the National Museum of Taiwan History. Look up: every square of the ceiling has a golden dragon in a blue circle.
